author: AtditC
body:
Hello Avicus Senior Staff.
Here's my 6th application for the Moderator rank:

Age: 16
Timezone: Central European Timezone
Do you have Teamspeak? Yes
Do you have Discord? Yes (Atdit#8333)
Do you have access to a recording software?
Yes. My recording software is probably the best one to use as a moderator and I can only recommend it to all other staff members.

I'm able to save the last 20 minutes of what happened on my display in a video. This software is called "ShadowPlay" which is a feature of NVIDIA GeForce Experience, and always running in the background. It worked great in the past and almost never let me down. It's even useful for non-moderators. Especially on TeamSpeak or on Discord where people can say/write something which is against the rules, and quickly delete it. I would still have the evidence. With this recording software I can basically record everything I want without having to open it first or pressing a button.


CRITERIA 1: SELF REFLECTION/EVALUATION

Do you have any experience as a moderator on other servers?
Yes, I do have a have experience as a moderator on another server, but not a Minecraft server. I once (~1-2 weeks ago) was Moderator on a Discord server with 500-1000 people. It might not be much, but I still learnt some stuff from my time over there.

I also was Jr. Mod on Avicus just about ~1 year ago, and failed my trial. I will talk more about this/mention it in the following questions. Of course, most of my moderating experience comes from the Jr. Mod trial, where I moderated for about 100 hours until my demotion.

What is your biggest weakness [...] 
(This will go a bit off topic, but I think it's important to understand the history behind my "biggest weakness")
My biggest weakness probably is, as you probably can tell by now, changing between being serious and joking around or even being toxic in some situations.

In the past few months I was banned twice on the official Avicus Discord. I can explain why I was banned and why I failed there. So the first time when I was banned, the reason was "being disrespectful/rude, and constantly starting flame wars" and I was banned for about 5 weeks. All this happened because I was pushing my (a bit more special) ideas about politics too far. I changed my avatar to stuff which could've annoyed people, and I also was rude "towards groups of people".
After this 5 week ban, I, of course, gave my best to stop being rude towards anyone, if it's directed or through talking about my political views, and I think I also achieved that for the most part, after I was unbanned. I also watched out that I wouldn't break any more rules on Discord, where I accidentally screwed up:

The second time I was banned, it was because I made a "ddos joke threat" (I said "I will ddos this discord if #politics won't come back.") The Senior(s) who punished me were aware that it was a joke, since it's almost impossible to ddos a Discord server. When I made the joke ddos threat I first thought about if I really should send this message, since I knew ddos threats are illegal, but I thought the staff team wouldn't punish me for it because they knew ddosing a Discord server is almost impossible and it therefore is only a joke. Well it turned out that it's not allowed to make joke ddos threats and I was banned for 14 days. I'm still surprised that I was banned 14 days for this joke threat, since it's a threat which didn't directly attack someone and nobody could've been really hurt.

When I was banned, I immediately thought about how my chances for the Staff applications sunk from "good" to "bad" in just a single moment. I didn't even try to appeal my ban, because I knew that it would only lead to more conflict, and that it would lower my chances even more if I'd fail. That's what I meant with "my biggest weakness is changing between being serious and not serious in certain situations".

[...] and how will it affect your moderating?
Well, to be honest, it shouldn't affect my moderating anymore because now that I have been punished so many times for breaking certain rules, I should be able to tell what I can do or post as a moderator and what not. 1 year ago, this weakness, however, affected me so much that I even got demoted from Jr. Mod - when I was a good in-game moderator,  but acting terrible towards others inside the staff team. Now, one year went over and I think it's fair to say that I'm also more mature about this. It's up to you if you are willing to give me another chance as a Jr. Mod.
I told you before in the previous question "Do you have any experience as a moderator on other servers?" that I was a moderator on a Discord server, which I was promoted to 3 months ago. (I just left this server for private reasons a few days/weeks ago) In this short time, I did a lot as moderator on this server and also earned some more experience on how to communicate with the staff team internally and how to interact with the community.

The proof that I can act maturely if I really want to is at my punishments page. The last punishment which I received ingame - not talking about TeamSpeak/Discord - was from stunning 2 years and 9 months ago, when I was 13 years old. It proves that I can be mature, since I played for over 1000 hours in game after my last punishment and didn't get a single warn for breaking any rule.


What qualities do you think a leader must have?
A leader must know how to deal with any situation or scenario that could happen and always has to act as a leader. A leader also must be mature, so others take the leader serious. A leader also must be constructive and treat everyone the same, no matter what kind of personal relation the leader has to a player.

Would you consider yourself a leader? Why/why not?
I do think that I have what it takes to be a leader. I already have quite some moderating experience from 11 months ago, and also know how the other moderators act in their leading position.


What attributes distinguish yourself from other players that qualify you to be a moderator?
1) Experience: I've been on Avicus since almost 4 years now and my total playtime is 1500+ hours. I know a lot about Avicus than most other players. I also have moderating experience from one year ago, when I was Jr. Mod for about 3 weeks.

2) Activity: I'm one of the most active players of Avicus. When I used to be Jr. Mod ~1 year ago, I used to be the most active user & staff member for 3 weeks until my demotion. I had an average online time per day of about 4-6h. ~30-40h per week, and this in average while I also had about 8 hours school per day. That also shows how much I love moderating and how much motivation I have.

3) Technical skills & Computer knowledge: I've been with computers since many, many years and know also know a lot about Minecraft, TeamSpeak & Discord, which all are Avicus platforms. I have a lot of preknowledge from moderating, not only on Avicus but also on Discord. If a player has a problem with his Discord/TeamSpeak client or a question about Minecraft settings generally, I most likely can help them.


What skills do you believe you should have when interacting with the community?
When interacting with the community the most important points are to be fair, to respect and treat everyone the same and not to prejudge based on your experience. Also, you need the skills of behaving and acting as a staff member at any time, which means you can't just do what you want anymore. You need to look professional to the community and not use curse words too often, if at all. Also, you need to take other players serious as you are in a staff position which means you can't joke around whenever you like to.

Do you believe you have these skills?
Yes, I do think that I can act and behave as a moderator, as I already have experience on Avicus and a Discord server. I learned these skills from just watching how other Mods & Sr. Mods moderate the server and talk to the community, when I was Jr. Mod myself 11 months ago, and from my Moderater time on a Discord server.


What in your opinion are the three main character traits a moderator must have when moderating?
1) Confidence: A moderator must be confident about their moderating. The moderator must be confident when he is moderating.

2) Objectivity: A moderator must judge situations always objectively. As an example, he can't prejudge someone because he has a bad personal experience with this player.

3) Responsibility: A moderator must of course be responsible for his actions, and deal with appeals, feedback and complaints which he can and most likely will receive sooner or later.


CRITERIA 2: GENERAL SITUATIONS

You notice a moderator giving out a lot of false bans. They almost always have insufficient evidence or sometimes no evidence and they don’t seem to care. You notice it but other staff members don’t. What would you do?
I would first tell this staff member what I think about his bans and about the insufficient evidence he uses. If he doesn't change and doesn't improve, I will contact the Senior Moderators with some proof of my claims. If they won't do anything, I will try to contact an Admin and tell him about it. There isn't much else I can do.


You are in Teamspeak with a few other players and they begin talking quite disrespectfully about a particular staff member. You agree with what they’re saying to an extent, but the conversation starts to become racial and very disrespectful soon after. You are all in a nightclub channel where this is allowed. What would you do?
Since "heavy bullying", "racism" and "harassment" aren't allowed in Nightclubs, I will warn them. If they won't calm down, I will warn or even kick them again, if they will continue, I'll punish them depending on how bad exactly they acted with either a tempban for at least a few hours or even a few days. Also, I would inform the targeted staff member after this so he is up to date on what people think and talked about him.


You are in an Avicus team. One of your teammates is also an Avicus Staff member. One day in your team discord the team member/staff member posts a screenshot of a thread that only staff members can see. The content in the screenshot isn’t very important/confidential but only staff members could see it on the forums. If anything, what would you do?
I don't know if it matters if minor stuff gets accidentally leaked, but it will probably result in a warning for the staff member, so I would send a message to a Senior Mod about this. I'm not sure what the rules about leaking are, because they're not listed on a public Avicus thread. Generally, I always would contact staff members in higher positions when I don't know what to do in a situation like this, because it's important to learn from more experienced staff members and not to screw up, especially as a Jr. Mod.


Some senior staff members are in teamspeak joking around with each other. They are removing others ranks, creating certain channels and even harassing certain users. They don’t mean any harm but some players in the channel feel a bit angry that they are using their permissions the way they are. What would you do?
I would try to make them realize that some players are feeling angry and annoyed by this, and maybe send them a message or two. I'm pretty sure all of the current Sr. Mods wouldn't do stuff like that, but if some would, I would just simply report it to a higher staff member, in this case, an Admin.


CRITERIA 3: OTHER
NOTE: This is a new criteria and these questions are less to do with right/wrong answer and more to do with us getting to know you. Please answer these honestly. There is no right or wrong answer.


Why do you want to be a moderator?
There are a lot of reasons why I want to be a moderator. I think the most important one is because I want to help the players who as an example get killfarmed by hackers in a public game and literally can't do anything against it unless a staff member is online. I want to help the activity of the staff team to make this server better and might help a bit in saving it from dying. Avicus is very strong, and still is online, although a lot of people predicted that it would be gone by now, but it's not and I think we can reverse that process if we work on it hard enough.
Another reason why I want to be a moderator is because I simply like law & order, everywhere. It's always nice when you can play on a server with fair rules and know that there are staff members who watch out that everything works fine, as it's supposed to be.


What does Avicus mean to you?
Avicus means a lot to me. I've been playing since 4 years on this server and I think I wouldn't be playing Minecraft today if Avicus wasn't around. I love playing with friends or solo in both public games and scrims. It's just fun. I like the unique style of Avicus too. I also want to mention that I donated over 250-280$ for this server in total, having done 4 Giveaways, donated for friends and myself etc.. 


Anything specific the staff team could do better?
Yes, I think the Senior Staff team should watch out for their moderators and make sure they act & behave as Moderators should (or make it more strict). I recently saw one, two moderators who should've calmed down a bit on using caps and spamming. The other thing would be staff activity. Sometimes, there are no mods on the server, which can be very annoying. Apart from these things, I think the staff team does a great job and improved a lot in the previous months/previous year.


Why did you choose to apply at Avicus?
Because Avicus is my favorite network. Not only gaming network, but network generally. There are a lot of nice people in the community. I also like the "style" of Avicus, the kind of "simplicity" on Avicus, especially compared to other, bigger servers. Avicus also needs more moderators, which can play at times when no other moderators would be on. I think I will be a good addition to the staff team.


Do you have anything else to add to your application?
Yes, quite some stuff.

1) Usually when a player gets a lot of punishments in the previous x weeks or months, he most likely won't get accepted when applying for staff. I remember when TheMasterClock returned to Avicus and for some reason wanted to get kicks, tempbans etc. ingame. When the Staff Apps opened and he got accepted for a Jr. Mod trial, I was surprised (I think it was a "staff reassessment, whatever that is.), but I was even more surprised when I saw how he quickly he changed from a "bad player" with a lot infractions to a good player who helps the server.
If I will get a Jr. Mod trial, I will prove you that I'm also able to improve and leave my bad habits behind me, just like TheMasterClock did, because I take being a staff member serious.

2) German moderators: There are currently 0 native German speaking staff members, as far as I know. I think it's important that the staff team should have moderators with a diverse language spectrum, to optimize communication between the staff and community. I am from Switzerland and therefore a native German speaker.

3) I want to point out that there are currently not a lot Moderators in the staff team (14 Mods, 2 Jr. Mods) and that it sometimes still happens that no staff members are online at certain times. Back in my Jr. Mod trial, I always gave my best in being active when there were no other staff members online. I was always there when no one else was, because I know how it feels like when you're being killed from a player 100 blocks away and you can't enjoy the game.

4) This is a small note I want to make regarding to my previous denial of my staff application back in April. I was denied for "Poor behavior towards others." and the main reason behind that was because I played a joke racist song on TeamSpeak in a Nightclub channel, when racism wasn't allowed, which resulted in a 24h ban. The other two Discord bans which I had a few weeks / months ago were for other reasons. They were because I made a joke ddos threat and because I started flame wars & being disrespectful, but not racist or anything similar to that. (I obviously learned from the TeamSpeak ban.)

5) Becoming a moderator, or at least receiving a second Jr. Mod trial chance would mean everything to me. 1 year ago, in the night before the day I was having my Interview, I was so excited and nervous about it that I couldn't sleep for 30 minutes. I tried everything. Listening to music, changing bedrooms, changing positions etc. but I just couldn't sleep because the Interview on the following day was making me so nervous. This day then became the happiest day I ever had on Avicus, as I was being promoted to Jr. Mod.
The following day, I printed out the rule page, punishment guidelines and staff page which I would always have next to me while moderating, to help me get started.

6) I split some questions up in two parts, to make it more organized.

Greetings,
-Atdit

replies.body: [Reviewing] - Your application has been tagged reviewing and will remain like this until at least 4 other Senior Staff & Mentors read over your application and vote.
replies.body_tagged: [Reviewing] - Your application has been tagged reviewing and will remain like this until at least 4 other Senior Staff & Mentors read over your application and vote.

replies.author: _DISTRACTION_
replies.body: Apologies for the late response. I'm really not sure of why nobody has given you one, as all the votes have been in since late September. The majority of the mentors and senior staff team voted to deny this application, with a common reason being that they want to see you act professionally & politely over a long period of time (and not only during application periods).
